major_concerns: Task corpus may not represent vendor/device corner cases (external validity).
RAG retrieval-corpus quality could confound effect attributed to verifier.
Verifier rule coverage (which checks count as ‘critical’) is underspecified.
Human criticality labels are subjective and not validated for inter-rater reliability.
required_design_repairs: Specify retrieval corpus construction and provide public snapshot/hash.
Enumerate verifier rule-set and map verifier failures to operational-critical categories; publish rule definitions.
Increase task diversity across vendors/protocols or justify representativeness; include external-validation subset.
Define human-annotation protocol and report inter-rater agreement; consider larger annotation sample or automated proxies.
Add explicit limitations on single-LLM generality or include at least one additional model for sensitivity checks.

major_concerns: Baseline (LLM self-correction without verifier) may be an unrealistic strawman unless carefully specified.
Verifier counterexamples may vary in informativeness; repair success may depend heavily on prompt engineering.
Risk of overfitting repairs to counterexample phrasing rather than underlying bug class.
Iteration budget (≤2) may miss long-tail repairs.
required_design_repairs: Precisely define the self-correction baseline prompts and justify as a realistic operator workflow.
Pre-register prompt templates for repair and critique steps; include ablation documenting prompt sensitivity.
Specify measures to detect overfitting to counterexample wording (e.g., held-out failure types).
Justify iteration budget or include exploratory arm with extended iterations and report diminishing-return analysis; disclose when exploratory results are used.

major_concerns: Latency/resource measurements rely on proxies and may not reflect production retrieval/verifier services.
Chosen SLA thresholds appear arbitrary without operator-context justification.
Concurrent-load simulation may not capture realistic operator request patterns or network conditions.
No clear plan to emulate network/service variability (e.g., retrieval cache hits/misses).
required_design_repairs: Justify SLA thresholds via citation or operator survey, or present results across multiple threshold choices.
Instrument and report retrieval and verifier microbenchmarks; include sensitivity analysis varying retrieval/verifier latencies.
Describe concurrency simulation model and validate it against a plausible operator workload; consider trace-driven simulation if available.
Report resource-proxy limitations and, where possible, complement with lightweight containerized service examples to approximate production behavior.

major_concerns: Metric thresholds and definitions may require post-hoc calibration, risking circularity.
Human-annotation sample (n=50) is small for robust agreement estimates.
Correlation with verifier severity is associative and may not establish operational causality.
Metric sensitivity to topology encoding and verifier granularity is not controlled.
required_design_repairs: Pre-register exact metric definitions, thresholds, and calibration procedure; if calibration required, treat as exploratory and report separately.
Increase human-label sample or report inter-rater reliability and confidence intervals; pre-specify rater selection and training.
Include stratified evaluation across topology families and report metric stability; add external validation split.
State explicitly that metric–verifier relationships are correlational and propose follow-up causal tests; if possible, add small causal perturbation checks (e.g., targeted config variants).
